description: In Mixed Data Interpretation (Mixed DI), two or more types of graphs, such as Pie Charts, Tables, or Bar Graphs, are presented together to analyze information. Solving these questions requires basic mathematical skills and establishing a relationship between the given graphs.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: It is essential to understand the combinations of graphs used in Mixed DI.

key_concepts.explanation: In this combination, the pie chart shows the percentage or degree distribution of the total value, and the table shows the sub-classification of that data, such as a male/female ratio.
One graph represents the absolute value or quantity, while the other graph displays the percentage change or another related variable.
The connecting link between both graphs. This could be a year, department, or company whose data is represented in both places.

sections.title: Essential Formulas
sections.description: Important mathematical formulas to speed up data interpretation and calculation.

equations: Percentage Increase = ((Final Value - Initial Value) / Initial Value) * 100
Percentage Decrease = ((Initial Value - Final Value) / Initial Value) * 100
Ratio of A and B = A / B
Average = Sum of all quantities / Total number of quantities

sections.title: Steps for Data Extraction
sections.description: A step-by-step method to extract information from both graphs to solve questions accurately.

steps.title: Identify the Base Value
steps.detail: First, check what the total sum or base value of each graph is. The base values of both graphs can be the same or different.

steps.title: Establish Relationship
steps.detail: Find the common variable present in both graphs. For example, if a pie chart shows 'total employees in departments', the table might show 'number of males in departments'.

steps.title: Sequence of Calculation
steps.detail: Calculate the final value directly. Avoid extracting intermediate values separately unless explicitly asked in the question.

sections.title: Important Cases
sections.description: Special types of patterns asked in exams and the conditions to solve them.

cases.condition: When base values of both graphs are different
results: Direct addition or subtraction of percentage or degree cannot be done.
The actual value must be calculated first before performing any mathematical operations.

cases.condition: When one graph is in percentage and the other in whole numbers
results: Find the 100% or total value of the percentage graph using the whole number data.
Bring both data sets into the same unit for comparison.

sections.title: Time Management and Techniques
sections.description: Effective strategies to quickly solve Mixed DI questions.

key_concepts.explanation: To avoid lengthy calculations, convert numbers to their nearest round values. (Example: Calculate 24.8% as 25% if the multiple-choice options are far apart).
When the final answer is asked in percentage or ratio, directly use the ratios instead of calculating the actual values.
